atoms.a: What happens to your breathing and heart rate during exercise?

feedback.finish: During exercise, your breathing and heart rate increases. This is because your muscles are working harder and need more oxygen to be carried to them through the bloodstream.

atoms.a: What is the throbbing movement of blood through your body called?

feedback.finish: You can easily feel your pulse by touching certain parts of your body, such as your wrists and neck. Each beat of your pulse is one beat of your heart.

hint.text: Your resting heart rate is how many times your heart beats per minute when you are at rest. You can measure it by counting the beats of your pulse.
hint.label: Resting heart rate

atoms.a: If the average resting heart rate for a child is 60-110 beats per minute, what might it be during exercise?

feedback.wrong: Your heart rate increases during exercise, but also won’t go much higher than around 200 beats per minute.

instruction.text: This line graph shows Luca’s heart rate during a run around the school field. Look at the line graph and answer the questions.

atoms.a: What is Luca’s resting heart rate?
atoms.hint: Luca’s heart rate is at rest before he starts the run.

atoms.a: Between which minutes was Luca’s heart rate highest?

feedback.end: This is when Luca’s body was working hardest to pump blood to his muscles.

atoms.a: When does Luca’s heart rate begin to decrease?

feedback.end: After 4 minutes of running, Luca starts to wind down and recover. This means that his heart does not need to work as hard to provide his muscles with oxygen.

instruction.text: Luca’s teacher, Mr Taylor, completes the same run around the field. Look at the line graph and answer the questions.

atoms.a: Who has a lower resting heart rate?

feedback.end: Mr Taylor has an older heart than Luca. Therefore, oxygen is pumped more slowly around his body.

atoms.a: Whose heart rate increased most sharply?

feedback.end: Mr Taylor’s heart rate quickly escalated between the first and second minutes of running. Here, his heart was pumping intensely to get oxygen to his muscles.

atoms.a: When does Mr Taylor begin his recovery?

feedback.end: Mr Taylor begins his recovery 2 minutes earlier than Luca. His heart rate decreases from 150 bpm to 60 bpm.

atoms.a: Who do you think has a higher level of fitness?

feedback.end: Luca’s heart rate is much more stable than Mr Taylor’s and reaches a lower maximum. This indicates that his heart and lungs are healthier and do not need to work as hard to circulate blood.
